besluite.rede: 'maar 'n dier met vlerke van vel' has no verb of its own, so the AWS rule for a comma joining two sentences does not apply, and the double 'nie' already marks the contrast clearly.

Putting the prepositional phrase after 'gebou het' is normal, natural Afrikaans and keeps 'dele' next to its relative clause; the proposal is only a different word order, and it matches the wording of the 'meganies' glossary entry less closely.

besluite.fout: 'werk ook by dinge wat vlieg' is vague and leans on English 'work with/apply to'.
besluite.rede: The fault is real, but in the proposal 'raaksien' lands after the relative clause ('wat vlieg raaksien'), which makes a Grade 5 reader stumble, and it narrows 'apply to' to 'see', so the writer should fix it another way.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two sentences, each with its own subject and verb ('n donker voel ... is'; 'jou oog kry').
besluite.rede: Required comma under the AWS 2017; nothing else changes.
Using 'een' as a noun substitute ('n meganiese een') is ordinary Afrikaans, so the proposal is a lateral rewording.

besluite.fout: The trailing 'uit hierdie kwartaal se kunsklas' attaches to 'iets wat vlieg', so the sentence can be read as something flying out of the art class.
besluite.rede: Splitting the sentence removes the misreading, keeps 'model' and the same meaning (the learner's own work from this term's class), and leaves two shorter sentences.

besluite.fout: 'Kyk so' is flat and can read as a casual 'just look', not 'look in the same way'.
besluite.rede: 'Kyk net so' clearly means 'in the same way, with the same steps', and it still points back correctly after change 6.
